answers: acceptance-gate finding 1: not mine — the finding reports that no test file contains assertions tagged with the design's SPEC ids (DSPRB-1 through DSDEL-1, DSADR-3, DSBUD-1). Writing test assertions and tagging them with SPEC ids is the test-author's responsibility, not the design's. My design correctly defines every SPEC with its id, Given/When/Then contract, and `covers:` mapping. The test-author stage is the output that must carry those tags into test files.

acceptance-gate finding 2: not mine — the reachability check failing for `scripts/lib/compat.sh` and `scripts/lib/helpers.sh` is a downstream consequence of the same missing test files: without any tagged test assertions, the pipeline has no test to fail when it reverts those files. My `WIRING: none` declaration is correct on its own terms: the probe variables are set and consumed entirely within the library files being modified; no external file calls the new probe behavior directly; external callers reach `zbuild_sed_inplace` and `_zb_target_mode_v` through unchanged function names. `WIRING: none` requires no change.
